nodes.name: Every 2 minutes (7am-7pm PT)
nodes.notes: Switched from a plain 2-min interval + downstream IF gate to a cron expression restricted to hours 7-18 (2026-08-19, per Justin's ask, once he confirmed this workflow's own Settings > Timezone is set to America/Los_Angeles). n8n evaluates a Schedule Trigger's cron against the WORKFLOW's configured timezone (this one, not the n8n instance's global default), so this now correctly means 7am-7pm Pacific without needing an explicit setZone() downstream. */2 7-18 * * * fires every 2 min from 7:00 to 18:58 -- last fire before 7pm, matching the prior IF-gate's `hour < 19` cutoff exactly. IMPORTANT: this only stays correct as long as Settings > Timezone on this workflow stays set to America/Los_Angeles -- if that ever gets cleared or changed, this cron silently starts firing on Pacific-labeled hours in whatever timezone replaces it.

nodes.name: Create draft message
nodes.notes: Creates the message as a DRAFT rather than calling /sendMail directly. Graph's /sendMail returns 202 with no body, so there's no way to get the message id/conversationId/webLink back from it -- creating the draft first gives us those in the response, then 'Send draft message' actually sends this exact message. continueOnFail is on so one bad address doesn't kill the whole run; 'Draft created OK?' checks whether this actually succeeded.

nodes.name: Draft created OK?
nodes.notes: Checks $json.id rather than a string-empty operator -- if 'Create draft message' failed, continueOnFail replaces $json with {error:...} (per the same pattern documented in resolve_thread.nodes.js), so $json.id is undefined and this coerces to 0/false either way. Same gt-0 shape as 'Any valid leads?' above, already proven in workflow 2.

nodes.name: Send draft message
nodes.notes: If this call fails after the draft was already created (rare -- transient Graph error), the draft is left sitting unsent in the mailbox and qualifying_email_status stays 'pending', so next run tries this lead again and creates a second draft. Mild Drafts-folder clutter on repeated failure, not a duplicate send -- acceptable tradeoff, revisit only if it turns out to happen often.
